bot_carry_v1.method:
Sizing: capital $10,000 (config.py:12). Notional = capital x CARRY_NOTIONAL_X 1.0 (config.py:17; runner.py:52-54 sets allocation_pct 100 and leverage 1.0; trades.py:192 gives size_usdt = capital x alloc/100 x lev = $10,000, which matches live SJ-4242 at size_usdt 10000). So % of capital equals % of notional.

What the live bot books at close (trades.py:601-607): net_pct = accrued SHORT-side funding - (ENTRY_EXIT_COST_PCT 0.20 + CARRY_SLIPPAGE_PCT 0.04), charged once per trade. pnl_usdt = size_usdt x net_pct/100. Funding comes from funding.accrued_pct over (entry, exit], using settlement rows only (timestamp % 28800 = 0), with positive rates paid to the short leg (funding.py:112-118,138). No price P&L, stop, target, time stop, tilt or cooldown. The only extra rule is one action per UTC day.

Signal: I replayed the live sleeve's decide() logic on the study's daily funding sums:
- Complete days only; today excluded (signal.py:89; funding.py:174-175).
- At least 8 complete daily records before any evaluation (signal.py:126).
- Entry when the 7-day mean > 0, no trade is open and the exit condition is NOT active (signal.py:246-247).
- Exit when the last 30 daily sums total < -0.5 % (signal.py:131-139, 235-244).
- A decision on complete day D acts on the first tick of D+1 (modelled as 00:00:60 UTC). Funding is summed over settlements strictly after entry, up to and including the exit tick.

Result per completed episode = sum(rate x 100) - 0.24. The one completed episode: 7.8607 gross - 0.24 = 7.6207.

The still-open episode (2020-04-16 onward, +72.88 % net marked at 2026-09-11) is excluded because it is not a closed trade. Other conventions, shown for transparency and NOT included:
- Study state machine as coded, full history, 0.24 cost: 7.6999, -0.2489, -0.2100, -0.2552, then open +72.86.
- Study scoring window at the study's actual 0.20 cost: 5.7169, -0.2089, -0.1700, -0.2152, then open +72.90. This reproduces the 5 round trips.
- Live sleeve on prod.db funding (history starts 2019-09-25): 7.2922.
bot_carry_v1.caveats:
1) The baseline has n = 1 and is statistically unusable. Every resampled mean equals 7.62, so the 10th percentile is 7.62. Any closed carry trade below +7.62 % of capital would go AMBER, whether or not anything is wrong.

2) The single completed trade is left-censored. It entered on the first day the rule could be evaluated, so its size depends on where the funding history starts, not on the strategy. Moving the start or changing the boundary convention gives 7.29 to 7.70. There is no research episode with a natural entry AND a natural exit under the live rule.

3) The only other episode is right-censored: open since 2020-04-16, about 2,340 days, +72.9 % net. The live rule exited once in 7 years (cum30 < -0.5 % only on 2020-03-31 to 2020-04-14). By construction every rule exit happens inside a sustained negative-funding stretch. A live closed trade is therefore expected to be rare, and to reflect how long the trade was held more than any edge.

4) Live sleeve vs study state machine: the study enters on 'corner' days (7-day mean > 0 while the 30-day exit is still active) and exits the next day (run_p2_exit_rules.py:67-68). That produced 3 extra one-day round trips on 2020-04-08, -10 and -12, each about -0.21 to -0.26 %. The sleeve waits instead (signal.py:246-247; tests/test_carry_exit_rule.py:126-137 and 202-238). Those trades are excluded because live does not take them. So the 5 toggles in the study's CUM-30D row, repeated in docs/calibration/carry.md:29, describe the study state machine; the live sleeve has one exit.

5) Boundary timing is approximate to within one settlement (about 0.01 %). Live collects from the 08:00 print after a 00:00 entry and may include the exit-day 00:00 print, depending on feed lag; the study collects the 00:00 print at entry and not at exit. The sleeve also needs spot and perp daily closes to be present (signal.py:89-90). I did not replay that: cd_spot_binance and cd_futures_ohlcv cover the whole window, but daily gaps inside them were not checked.

6) Delta-neutral assumption: like the live bot, this ignores basis, spot/perp mark-to-market and margin effects. The funding source is Binance BTCUSDT only.

7) Pre-2026-04-25 cd_funding_rate rows are hourly CryptoDataDownload bars filtered to settlement hours. They are identical to the Binance API settlement values on every shared timestamp, so data-source risk is low.
bot_carry_v1.notes:
RECOMMENDATION: the per-trade AMBER test does not work for carry, so the dashboard should skip it (for example, require at least 10 research trades, or exclude open-ended, no-stop variants). The only research baseline is one left-censored episode. Live bot_carry_v1 has 0 closed trades: SJ-4242 has been open since 2026-07-22 13:54 UTC, $10,000 notional, and would book +0.759 % of capital if closed now (+0.9992 % funding over 162 settlements to 2026-09-14 08:00, minus 0.24). Under the current rule it should stay open until a 30-day cumulative funding below -0.5 %, which happened once in 7 years.

ALTERNATIVE REFERENCE, if the operator wants a carry warning: accrued funding per 30-day block while the live sleeve holds, in % of capital (no costs inside a block). This is computable live from the open trade with funding.accrued_pct. On the cache series with the live-sleeve hold mask (held 99.2 % of settlements), there are 82 non-overlapping 90-settlement blocks from 2019-10 to 2026-08:
- Full history: mean 0.991, median 0.550, p10 0.145, p5 -0.073, min -0.232; 7.3 % of blocks negative.
- Post-ETF (2024-01-11 onward, 32 blocks): mean 0.568, p10 -0.039, min -0.232. The 2026-02 to 2026-04 blocks were -0.060, -0.089 and -0.232.
- p10 of the mean of k blocks, iid bootstrap with seed 42 (full / post-ETF): k=1 0.144 / -0.060; k=2 0.247 / 0.152; k=3 0.315 / 0.223; k=6 0.433 / 0.300; k=12 0.568 / 0.366.

The iid bootstrap ignores funding-regime persistence: 2021 blocks run up to 7.3 %. The multi-block p10s are therefore too narrow, and post-ETF is the more relevant regime. All block values are printed by carry_blocks.py in the scratch dir.

SIDE FINDING (documentation, not acted on): the CUM-30D study says every toggle was charged 0.24 % (findings.md:11, README.md:6 and :19, docs/calibration/carry.md:16). The simulator it imports unchanged actually charges 0.20 %: run_c2_carry_timing.py:15 sets COST_RT = 0.002, used at :50, and it is imported at run_p2_exit_rules.py:17 and :91. The saved results confirm it: gross minus net is 0.950 %/yr at 4.751 round trips/yr for LIVE and 0.149 at 0.742 for CUM30D, both exactly 0.20 per round trip. At the stated 0.24, LIVE would be about 10.66 %/yr and CUM30D about 11.55. CUM30D's advantage over the old streak exit would widen from +0.74 to about +0.89 %/yr, so the verdict does not change, but the three documents misstate the cost that was charged.
